To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
stimulation of B lymphocytes with B cell growth factors is associated with a modest increase in intracellular Ca2+ in distinct but overlapping subsets of B cells.

stimulation of human B cells with high molecular weight or low molecular weight human B cell growth factor, but not IL-4, IL-2, or interferon gamma, is associated with a modest increase in intracellular free calcium, which is distinct from that seen upon activation by anti-Ig.

stimulation of resting B cells by Staphyloccocus aureus Cowan (Sac) or anti-Ig is associated with increases intracellular calcium, while stimulation of activated B cells by high or low molecular weight growth factor is associated only with modest increases in intracellular cailcium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of intracellular calcium in the regulation of the B cell activation and proliferation.
the mechanisms of B cell activation and proliferation.
the mechanisms of signal transduction in B cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the induction of proliferation of human B cells by HMW- or LMW- BCGF is associated with an elevation of intracellular calcium in subpopulations of resting B cells which is modest compared with that induced by anti-Ig.
increases in intracellular Ca are not a universal phenomenon in human B cells, and that the effect of increasing calcium is dependent on the type of B cell and the type of stimulus.
increases in intracellular Ca2+ occur during activation and proliferation of human B lymphocyte subpopulations, and that the increases are associated with different subsets of B cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
B cells have a number of different mechanisms for increasing intracellular calcium, and these different mechanisms are utilized by B cells in different stages of their life cycle.

the activation of B cells by cross-linking of surface Ig is associated with increases of approximately 300 to 400 nM in intracellular calcium which occur in all resting B cells, and that the induction of proliferation of activated B cells by HMW- and LMW-BCGFS, but not IL-4, IL-2, or interferon gamma, is associated with increases which are smaller (approximately 100 to 150 nM) but are also seen in distinct but overlapping subsets
B cells have multiple calcium-regulated pathways, and that these pathways can be activated by distinct stimuli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
B cells are not a homogenous population, and that B cell growth factors can induce distinct responses in different subsets of B cells.
the induction of proliferation in resting B cells is not associated with increases in calcium.
increases in intracellular Ca2+ are associated with both activation and proliferation of human B cells, but that the subpopulations of cells responding to the various stimuli are not identical.
